A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge management is a social and organizational process, which can be supported by information and communication technologies, but cannot be reduced to them.

we have found that knowledge management technology can reproduce knowledge work practices, but only in the absence of the circuits of reproduction that are necessary for the reproduction of knowledge itself.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the circuits of reproduction in which work practices are embedded need to be taken into account in the design, development and evaluation of information systems.
work practice should be understood as a dynamic process of reproduction.

the implementation of knowledge management technology is a process that involves the reproduction of knowledge workers' practices, and that the success of this process is dependent on a deep understanding of the circuits of reproduction of the work practices of knowledge workers.
